title: Pilot quantization KPI triage and ramp plan
summary: Weekly sync for INT8/FP8 pilot. Reviewed latest KPI deltas (latency, throughput, quality), prioritized regression signals, agreed on short-term tuning and a 2-week ramp plan. Action items: additional eval slices, run 5x sample A/B with real traffic window, and updated benchmark CSV shared.
next_steps: Redwood: push updated benchmark CSV and quantization configs to shared drive by 2026-12-11
Customer: run A/B tests on morning traffic window (12/14–12/16) and share results
Schedule mid-pilot call for 2026-12-16 to review A/B outcomes and decide rollout
action_items: Liam: run cross-seed synthetic sensitivity sweep for two problematic intents (due 2026-12-13)
Jordan: share 3 anonymized intent slices that show downstream quality regressions (due 2026-12-12)
Elena: enable VM-level metrics and expose NVLink perf counters to Redwood log sink (due 2026-12-15)
transcript:
00:00:00 - Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. short agenda: delta review, triage, next steps. we have about 50 minutes.
00:00:12 - Jordan (Orion): yep, thanks Maya. running a bit late this morning, appreciate it.
00:00:21 - Liam (Redwood SE): quick note — we uploaded the latest bench CSV to the shared drive, filename bench-results-2026-12-08.csv. link in chat.
00:00:35 - Marcus (Orion CTO): saw that, thanks. initial read looked... okay but a couple of spikes on 95th pctl.
00:00:47 - Maya: perfect, can we start with the latency/throughput deltas INT8 vs FP8? Liam, take it away.
00:00:55 - Liam: yeah. so, baseline float16 on your infra for the model averaged 32ms p50, 120ms p95 for the test profile. INT8 gives p50 28ms, p95 110ms in our short tests, so about 10-15% tail reduction on that node. FP8 is closer to INT8 on p50 but we saw more variance on p95 depending on sequence length and kvcache hit patterns.
00:01:28 - Elena: when you say variance, is that network or kernel-level? we saw NVLink saturation that might align with the long seq lanes.
00:01:40 - Liam: mostly kernel and memory bandwidth. some of the quant kernels do more memcpy for dequant/decode for certain ops; on small batches it's fine, on long context with contention it shows up.
00:01:56 - Jordan: ok — how about quality? we are seeing a small uptick in mis-class for intent routing with INT8 on our sample set.
00:02:07 - Priya: we dug in — the top-3 intents affected are things with rare tokens and long context dependencies. the SNR drops are subtle but show in our eval.
00:02:21 - Marcus: can you show an example?
00:02:26 - Jordan: sure, I pulled a couple. (silence) um, in utterance A, float produces 'schedule-refill' but INT8 gives 'general-inquiry' which routes to a different workflow. leads to wrong downstream API call.
00:02:43 - Liam: thanks. that matches the token-saturation case. we think two knobs to tweak: per-channel quant scale clipping and a small calibration sweep on activation ranges.
00:02:59 - Maya: also consider hybrid fallback. run INT8 for p50/p75 and fallback to FP16 for sequences over 512 tokens or when kvcache miss rate > X.
00:03:12 - Elena: fallback makes sense but we need deterministic routing for SLAs. can't have flapping between variants.
00:03:22 - Priya: agreed — we can implement stability gate: only flip to FP16 if two consecutive sequences for same session exceed thresholds.
00:03:33 - Jordan: how do we capture that in Redwood? is that policy something we set in the route config?
00:03:40 - Maya: yes, can codify as part of the rollout policy — sequence-length gate + quality fallback. we'll provide example config.
00:03:48 - Marcus: security question — if we use Redwood Dedicated or Private, how is the key handling for quant snapshots and logs? our compliance team will care about KMS.
00:03:59 - Priya: on Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM, logs only persisted in your VPC, and we can restrict export.
00:04:10 - Elena: OK good. please send the compliance checklist.
00:04:14 - Maya: will do. link to security brief in chat.
00:04:20 - (15s pause)
00:04:35 - Liam: moving back to perf — we ran an ensemble of seeds. interestingly FP8 shows a 6% throughput gain on average for batch sizes >8 but at small batch (1-2) it's nearly identical to INT8. so for your real-time traffic (mostly batch=1), difference is minimal.
00:05:02 - Jordan: most of our prod calls are batch=1 with a 30% burst pattern. concern is tail on bursts.
00:05:11 - Liam: for bursts we recommend adaptive batching with a 20ms collect window; that reduces p95 by 18% in lab.
00:05:21 - Marcus: that might conflict with our latency SLOs for interactive users though.
00:05:27 - Priya: we can do dynamic policy — collect only if queue depth > threshold, otherwise immediate. Redwood supports that in the runtime.
00:05:39 - Jordan: switching topics — accuracy deltas: can you quantify the observed NER/intent deltas as ROUGE or exact-match?
00:05:48 - Liam: we used EM for intents and F1 for NER. INT8: intent EM dropped 1.8% absolute on the full eval; FP8: 1.1% absolute. On the flagged slice (long context rare tokens) INT8 dropped 5.2% vs float, FP8 3.7%.
00:06:11 - Jordan: so FP8 is consistently better quality-wise but less consistent on p95; is that right?
00:06:18 - Liam: yeah—FP8 gives smaller per-token quant error in many layers but some kernels not as well optimized on your particular GPU/driver stack, so tail suffers.
00:06:30 - Elena: which GPU are we seeing this on? A100 or H2?
00:06:35 - Liam: your staging nodes are A100s with older driver 470.x; we recommend 525+ for FP8 kernels to unlock optimizations.
00:06:46 - Marcus: upgrading driver in production is a non-trivial change. we need an ops window.
00:06:50 - Maya: that factors into the ramp plan. we can propose incremental: start INT8 ramp on existing drivers for a small percent of traffic while schedule FP8 + driver upgrade in a second wave.
00:07:03 - Jordan: what about model variants? can we host both float and quant variants concurrently and route based on policy?
00:07:10 - Priya: yes Redwood runtime supports pinned variants. routing policy can be probabilistic or gated by session attributes.
00:07:18 - Liam: practical suggestion: run 5% of traffic on INT8 for 3 days, monitor key metrics (intent EM, p95 latency, error rate), then if stable move to 20%. FP8 ramp only after driver upgrades.
00:07:34 - Marcus: sounds reasonable. question: what thresholds do you recommend to auto-halt ramp?
00:07:40 - Liam: auto-halt triggers we recommend: intent EM drop >2% absolute on production slice for 30m or p95 increase >15% for 30m, or error-rate >0.5% above baseline.
00:07:54 - Jordan: can we get those as config examples?
00:07:57 - Maya: yes, we'll provide sample rollout policies.
00:08:04 - (Background typing)
00:08:16 - Elena: earlier you mentioned memcopy overhead — any short-term tuning to reduce that?
00:08:22 - Liam: two quicks: operator fusion on dequant path and a micro-quant tweak — reduce per-channel granularity for some layers which reduces overhead but may increase per-layer quant noise. tradeoff.
00:08:36 - Jordan: would that be the per-channel vs per-tensor decision?
00:08:40 - Liam: exactly. for embedding-heavy layers per-tensor is often fine. for attention projection we prefer per-channel.
00:08:49 - Marcus: any risk of model quality cliffs with per-tensor?
00:08:53 - Liam: possible on rare-case slices, so we need to run a sensitivity sweep.
00:08:58 - Maya: action: run cross-seed sensitivity for those two knobs. Liam owns.
00:09:05 - Jordan: let's talk about instrumentation — we need token-level SNR and routing-level traces to map regressions to model internals. do you capture that?
00:09:15 - Priya: Redwood Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns. for PII we can mask tokens; we support trace sampling.
00:09:25 - Elena: good — send configuration steps for trace sampling and masking.
00:09:30 - Maya: will do.
00:09:36 - (28s silence)
00:10:05 - Jordan: one weird data point — on 12/07 we had a spike in hallucinations for a certain prompt family after switching to INT8 in a small slice. logs show temperature and topk the same. any ideas?
00:10:18 - Liam: could be quant rounding affecting top-k logits distribution—small shifts push tokens over the threshold. we should compare logits histograms pre/post.
00:10:28 - Priya: we can produce per-token logits diffs for flagged examples. Jordan, please provide examples.
00:10:34 - Jordan: will do.
00:10:38 - Maya: note on hypothesis — also check softmax stability under quantization; we have a micro-test that isolates that. Liam to run.
00:10:46 - Liam: noted.
00:10:50 - (1m pause while attendees check dashboards)
00:11:52 - Marcus: quick procurement question: if we go Dedicated for pilot ramp, what's the timeline for reserved capacity?
00:12:01 - Maya: Dedicated seats typically 2–3 weeks for small pools if capacity available; Private on-prem would be longer (4–6 weeks).
00:12:09 - Marcus: is there a temporary burst option?
00:12:12 - Maya: yes, burst capacity for Dedicated can cover spikes while you do ramp.
00:12:17 - Elena: fine. now for compliance, we need SOC2 report and audit log format.
00:12:22 - Maya: sending SOC2 and the audit format link after call.
00:12:26 - Jordan: good.
00:12:29 - (15s)
00:12:44 - Liam: OK next: A/B test plan. propose a 5-day window, morning traffic only, with 1:1 exposure across sessions split. we'll compute weighted EM and p95 per-day.
00:12:58 - Jordan: can you do session-aware splits? some of our sessions are long-running.
00:13:04 - Liam: yes, session-aware split by session id. Redwood supports sticky routing.
00:13:10 - Marcus: what metrics we should log? intent EM, NER F1, p50/p95, error rate, and hallucination count (as judged by heuristics).
00:13:20 - Maya: plus infra counters: GPU util, NVLink, memory alloc failures. Elena to expose those counters.
00:13:27 - Elena: will add NVLink and cuda errors to the log sink.
00:13:31 - Jordan: do you have a recommended threshold for hallucination heuristics?
00:13:36 - Liam: heuristic: response contains entities inconsistent with prompt entities OR low softmax confidence and increased repetition. threshold tune will be in the bench.
00:13:47 - (small cross talk)
00:13:55 - Jordan: about the bench CSV — I noticed you included driver versions. what if we can't upgrade drivers right away?
00:14:03 - Liam: then stick to INT8-only ramp and defer FP8. FP8 gains are nice but driver upgrade is prerequisite for stable tails.
00:14:12 - Marcus: timeline then: INT8 ramp next week, FP8 in parallel once driver upgrade scheduled.
00:14:18 - Maya: we'll create a two-wave ramp plan doc.
00:14:21 - (5s)
00:14:27 - Jordan: one more ops nuance — our infra team wants to avoid frequent model pulls. can Redwood keep quant variants local to the node?
00:14:36 - Priya: yes, model caching and pinning is supported; you can set eviction policies.
00:14:42 - Elena: perfect.
00:14:45 - (1m)
00:15:45 - Liam: quick note — we identified three suspect layers that correlate with the largest token delta. switching those layers to per-tensor quant reduced deviance by ~1.6% on the flagged slice but cost some throughput.
00:15:59 - Jordan: so it's a targeted per-layer override?
00:16:02 - Liam: yes, Redwood supports layer-level quant overrides in the compile profile.
00:16:06 - Marcus: that seems like a good compromise.
00:16:10 - Maya: action: collect a list of candidate overrides and run sensitivity.
00:16:14 - Liam: I'll add that to the sweep.
00:16:17 - (30s)
00:16:48 - Jordan: about monitoring — will Redwood alert on EM drop or p95 regression?
00:16:54 - Maya: Redwood Console can create alerts; we can ship sample alert rules for intent EM and p95.
00:16:59 - Elena: make sure alerts map to pager rotations.
00:17:03 - Maya: yes, we can integrate with PagerDuty and send webhooks.
00:17:07 - (brief)
00:17:12 - Jordan: anything on cost delta? we estimate token cost reduction if INT8 is stable. numbers?
00:17:19 - Liam: rough rule: INT8 gives 20–30% token compute cost reduction depending on kernel mapping and batching. FP8 similar but depends on driver efficiency. we'll provide a per-scenario cost table.
00:17:33 - Marcus: please include expected cloud egress and storage impacts in the table.
00:17:38 - Maya: will include total cost of ownership pro forma for two waves.
00:17:42 - (30s)
00:18:12 - Jordan: we saw some sessions with cache miss thrash — is there tuning for KV cache TTL to improve hits?
00:18:20 - Liam: yes, tune prefix caching window and session affinity; for dialog apps longer TTL usually helps. but watch memory pressure.
00:18:29 - Elena: we'll expose KV cache hit rates.
00:18:32 - Priya: Redwood logs those metrics per-route.
00:18:36 - (brief)
00:18:41 - Jordan: let's recap proposed immediate plan: 1) run 5% INT8 A/B next week, 2) sensitivity sweep on per-layer/per-channel knobs, 3) driver upgrade planning for FP8 wave, 4) instrumentation and alert lists. correct?
00:18:58 - Maya: yes, that's it. plus we'll share configs and benchmark CSVs.
00:19:03 - Marcus: timeline: bench upload 12/11, sample slices 12/12, A/B 12/14–12/16, review 12/16.
00:19:12 - Maya: added to next steps.
00:19:15 - (45s)
00:20:00 - Liam: quick gotcha — on one test we saw reproducible hallucination when sequences had repeated system tokens; model conditioning interacts weirdly with quant. we'll add this to the regression hunt.
00:20:12 - Jordan: thanks — that was one of our prompts. we'll include more examples.
00:20:17 - Maya: wrap-up — I'll send a meeting note with action items and the two-wave ramp plan.
00:20:24 - Elena: please include the SOC2 and KMS integration notes.
00:20:28 - Maya: will do.
00:20:32 - Marcus: any blockers from Redwood side?
00:20:36 - Priya: none beyond needing the slices and permission to pull logs; also need a short ops window for driver upgrade if you agree FP8 wave.
00:20:46 - Jordan: we'll coordinate with ops.
00:20:50 - Maya: ok, thanks everyone. next call tentative 2026-12-16.
00:20:55 - (meeting ends early; final wrap chatter)
00:21:05 - Jordan: thanks all.
notes: Benchmark CSV: bench-results-2026-12-08.csv (uploaded to shared drive)
Rollout policy examples and auto-halt thresholds will be provided by Redwood
Security pack: SOC2, KMS integration checklist to be shared
